scenario.name: r-cd-fresh-install
scenario.description: A fresh install of the candidate creates the continuation storage correctly and serves. 🌊's ruling (room msg 1567073096706297887, 2026-11-03 07:09Z): fresh install is its own j12 corpus row, with an empty state dir, a disposable process and no model turn, kept separate from the stopped-seat restore receipt, which proves upgrade and recovery; they prove different paths, and neither row is satisfied until its own artifact exists. ClawSweeper's P1 on openclaw/openclaw#129388 (comment 5442236054) names the gap: the new authority storage, migration paths and public SDK exports lack complete fresh-install/upgrade evidence. One disposable gateway starts on a state directory the control created and proved empty, with a minimal config and no model sign-in. The control observes readiness (owned listener, /readyz, /startupz, hello-ok), the agent database created at OPENCLAW_AGENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 40 directly with no migration journal entry showing an upgrade path, session_recipient_authority with the byte-walked column hash 6ede42f5f5ea65007530f5f59da660e22bcab9d932ba3fae6639b848aee8eb7b, exactly one epoch row from sessions.create then a visibility narrowing (read read-only from outside the gateway, published as SHA-256 only), openclaw config validate on the fresh config, a clean SIGTERM stop, and cleanup of the disposable state with a signed cleanup receipt. It proves no upgrade path, no model turn and no delegate delivery.
scenario.notes: Fixture-gated: k6 cannot create a state directory or start, observe and stop a gateway, so the k6 entry fails closed and the executable control is scripts/run-fresh-install-control.mjs (see the product-path map, with j12 path:line anchors at 352f56029dc95c60149ab4aaa127226a861d0b3d, in scenarios/r-cd-fresh-install.js). Refusals before anything starts, each named in refusal.json: state-dir-not-empty (a fresh install starts from an empty state directory; the control creates it with one atomic mkdir, so an existing empty one is refused too, as state-dir-exists, and a run that loses that race after the guard stops as state-dir-changed); state-dir-live (the state directory is, is inside, or contains ~/.openclaw, ~/.openclaw-<profile>, ~/.clawdbot or the operator's $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR); port-in-use (and port-is-live for 18789 or a live config's port); stage-build-mismatch (the stage's dist/build-info.json commit is not the candidate); model-credentials-in-environment (the control's own environment carries a model credential, named by key, never by value). The gateway gets a cleared environment, an empty control-owned HOME and a private TMPDIR, so no credential reaches it from the environment or from a CLI credential file. The minimal config is gateway.mode local, the port, bind loopback, token auth with a fresh disposable token, agents.defaults.continuation.enabled true, and logging.file in the run's private directory (without it the product logs to the machine-wide /tmp/openclaw rolling file a live gateway of the same user also writes); it lives in the private artifact directory, outside the state directory, and is removed at cleanup. The product's shared /tmp/openclaw temp root has no override, so the control records its entry count before and after, ungraded. The artifact directory is compared with the live and state directories through symlinks. Receipts, each graded present and holding: runtime-build-info, state-dir-empty-proof, readiness, agent-schema-version (user_version 40, schema_meta schema_version 40 inserted once by canonical creation: created_at equals updated_at), no-upgrade-path (migration_runs holds exactly one run, the fresh boot's own once-per-database receipt node-desktop-stream-pairing-defaults-v1 completed with nothing retired, which also shows the gateway's startup prepared this state database; no migration_sources, no backup_runs, no agent database registered below 40, registration itself being the opener's choice and not graded; anything else is named by the SHA-256 of its id), authority-table-column-hash, authority-epoch-row-hash (0 rows before sessions.create, exactly 1 after the narrowing, bound to the created session key), no-model-sign-in (no credential key in the running gateway's /proc environ, HOME is the control's, no auth_profile_store row), config-validate (exit 0, valid true, the fresh config's path), clean-stop (SIGTERM through the gateway's own child handle, exit 0 within the grace, no SIGKILL, no missed shutdown deadline, listener released, no run process left but the compile-cache maintainer the entry detaches by design, which is counted apart and stopped at cleanup), timings, signed-cleanup-receipt (no run process, listener, state, gateway HOME, its TMPDIR or config remains; HMAC-SHA256 with a launcher-held key, hmac-sha256-proof-observer-key-v1). Verdict, from the signed record only: PASS-candidate needs every receipt present and holding. FAIL-candidate when a present receipt contradicts a fresh install (a gateway that never served, a wrong or migrated schema, an upgrade path in the journal, a missing or drifted authority table, not exactly one epoch row, a model credential or auth profile, an invalid config, an unclean stop, residue after cleanup). MISSING-candidate when a receipt is absent: nothing to judge. PARTIAL-candidate when everything holds but a bound is missing (unsigned record, dirty docs harness, a stage without a buildId to bind hello-ok to, timings not recorded, a recorded control error). Any missing receipt keeps the record below PASS-candidate. Only counts and SHA-256s leave the databases; no credentials and no database contents are published. The row stays MISSING until a run at j12 lands and is reviewed.
scenario.registryNotes: Bound issue karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs#536 (map: comment 6597622114). Presentation: openclaw/openclaw#129388 is 🌊's. Upgrade and recovery are proven by j12's stopped-seat restore receipt; this row proves the fresh-install path only and is never folded with it.

invocation.authority: sessions.create (no message, no title source: no model turn), then session.visibility.set(suggest); the narrowing advances (creates) session_recipient_authority
invocation.lifecycle: one disposable gateway, started on the empty state directory and stopped with SIGTERM; no restart
invocation.controlState: a state directory the control creates (one atomic mkdir), removed at cleanup; config, gateway HOME and TMPDIR in <artifact-dir>.private, removed at cleanup; the gateway log stays there with the raw output

expectedReceipts.name: runtime-build-info
expectedReceipts.description: The staged runtime's dist/build-info.json commit (must equal the candidate; the guard refuses otherwise), buildId and version. hello-ok's server.buildId must equal the staged buildId.

expectedReceipts.name: state-dir-empty-proof
expectedReceipts.description: The state directory listed after the control created it and before the gateway's first boot: zero entries and its mode. The gateway HOME is control-owned and empty; the minimal config is 0600, outside the state directory, with exactly the expected keys (SHA-256 of its bytes published, the token never).

expectedReceipts.name: readiness
expectedReceipts.description: The listener owned by the run's process (/proc), /readyz 200 ready:true, /startupz 200 started, and hello-ok with a bootId (SHA-256 published) and the staged buildId; plus whether the agent database existed at first readiness.

expectedReceipts.name: agent-schema-version
expectedReceipts.description: The fresh agent database's PRAGMA user_version (must be 40, OPENCLAW_AGENT_SCHEMA_VERSION at j12) and its schema_meta primary row: role agent, schema_version 40, the agent id, and created_at equal to updated_at (one insert by canonical creation, never a later migration bump).

expectedReceipts.name: no-upgrade-path
expectedReceipts.description: The state database's migration journal: migration_runs counted and classified (exactly one run, node-desktop-stream-pairing-defaults-v1, completed with nothing retired: the fresh boot's own receipt; any other run is named by the SHA-256 of its id), migration_sources and backup_runs counts (must be 0), and agent_databases rows for the agent registered below schema 40 (must be 0; whether it is registered at all is the opener's choice and is recorded, not graded). PRAGMA user_version of the state database is recorded (36 at j12), not graded.

expectedReceipts.name: authority-table-column-hash
expectedReceipts.description: session_recipient_authority exists, and the SHA-256 of its canonical projection (PRAGMA table_xinfo columns plus PRAGMA table_list strict and without-rowid flags) equals 6ede42f5f5ea65007530f5f59da660e22bcab9d932ba3fae6639b848aee8eb7b, the value SQLite reports for the DDL at src/state/openclaw-agent-schema.sql:142-147 at j12.

expectedReceipts.name: authority-epoch-row-hash
expectedReceipts.description: Authority rows read read-only from outside the gateway: 0 before sessions.create, the count after it, and exactly 1 after the narrowing, bound to the created session key. Only the SHA-256 of that key and of its epoch are published.

expectedReceipts.name: no-model-sign-in
expectedReceipts.description: The running gateway's /proc environ keys (never values) carry no model credential and its HOME is the control's empty directory; the fresh agent database has no auth_profile_store row; the control's own environment carried no model credential.

expectedReceipts.name: config-validate
expectedReceipts.description: `openclaw config validate --json` on the fresh config with the gateway's own environment: exit code, valid, whether the reported path is the fresh config, warning and issue counts, and the SHA-256 of its output (raw output private).

expectedReceipts.name: clean-stop
expectedReceipts.description: SIGTERM to the gateway through its own child handle; it exits 0 on its own within the grace, with no SIGKILL and no 'shutdown deadline reached before stop' line, the listener released and no process carrying the run marker left behind but the entry's detached compile-cache maintainer, counted apart.

expectedReceipts.name: timings
expectedReceipts.description: Boot (spawn to first full readiness), authority establishment, config validate, stop and total, in milliseconds.

expectedReceipts.name: signed-cleanup-receipt
expectedReceipts.description: Cleanup stops only processes carrying the run marker (identity re-verified before any signal), removes the state directory it created (re-identified by device and inode), the gateway HOME, its TMPDIR and the config, and records that none remain and the listener is gone. The whole observer receipt is HMAC-SHA256-signed (hmac-sha256-proof-observer-key-v1) with a launcher-held key the gateway never receives.

review.notes: The control writes a candidate receipt only. Folding it is a reviewed corpus step at j12. The row stays MISSING until that artifact exists, and it is never folded with the stopped-seat restore receipt.

liveRunSafety.notes: run-proof.sh and run-proofs.sh refuse orchestration-required rows, so a catalog or live-suite run never fires this control. The owner runs it by hand on a staged j12 runtime (docs/R-CD-FRESH-INSTALL-CONTROL.md). It never reads OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN or OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_WS, never touches a live gateway or a live state directory, and never signals a process it did not start. It needs no live session: its one session lives in the disposable state.
